description:
The cast for the upcoming live-action The Legend of Zelda movie is becoming clearer, and a report indicates that the legendary New Zealand actor Sam Neill, who died in July at the age of 78, has a role in the game-to-film adaptation.

Deadline reports that Neill, best known to audiences as Dr. Alan Grant in three Jurassic Park films, filmed his role in the Wes Ball-directed movie prior to his death. title: The Late Sam Neill’s Final Movie Might Be The Legend Of Zelda

author: Cameron Koch
description:
After soaring past an initial goal of $100,000, a Game Industry Hardship Fund bundle on Itch.io is now nearing $200,000 raised with seven days remaining.

The bundle has so far raised more than $163,000, and features 127 games for the minimum price of $10, with the proceeds going towards helping laid-off developers pay for everyday expenses. There are some bigger-name games included as well, including indie titles like Skatebird, A Short Hike, and Arranger.

It's the brainchild of Necrosoft Games director Brandon Sheffield and United Videogame Workers, a CWA union benefiting game developers, who in response to repeated waves of mass layoffs in the past two years wanted to offer affected developers a lifeline.
title: Indie Game Bundle Aiding Laid-Off Developers Is Nearing $200,000 Raised

author: Cameron Koch
description:
Peak, the mountain-climbing with friends "friendslop" title that sold more than 10 million copies in its first year, is set to receive its final major update on August 11, and it looks to be an appropriate challenge for seasoned scouts.

Dubbed The Final Ascent, the update will introduce two new late-game biomes, the Gloom and The Citadel, which will cycle out with the game's current Caldera and The Kiln biomes. A trailer for the update shows the Gloom to be a ghostly-looking swamp, while The Citadel looks to be a medieval fortress, complete with traps like swinging flails. As if that wasn't enough to overcome, the trailer teases a monster one can only assume will hunt players during their climb.

It's been a wild trail for Peak, a collaboration between de
title: Peak’s Final Major Update Will Add A Danger-Filled Dungeon

author: Andrew Hayward
description:
The ongoing collapse of the crypto gaming industry claimed another victim this week, with blockchain startup Proof of Play announcing its demise roughly one year after shutting down its flagship game, Pirate Nation.

Founded by FarmVille co-creator Amitt Mahajan, Proof of Play was one of the many companies that attempted to pair familiar, casual gameplay with crypto token incentives and player-owned assets in the form of NFTs--a premise that most gamers never warmed up to.

“When we started out, we believed games using blockchain tech had the potential to usher in a new, decentralized internet,” the team wrote Tuesday on X. “Ultimately, we couldn't build a product and sustainable business that proved out this thesis at scale.”

Launched in 2022, the browser-based Pirate Nation f
title: Another Blockchain Game Studio Shuts Down As Crypto Trend Sputters Out

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
The live-action The Legend of Zelda movie from Sony Pictures and Nintendo has already cast its Zelda and Link, but what about all the other roles? A new report claims that Australian actor Uli Latukefu, best known for the TV series Young Rock, will play the villain, Ganondorf.

This is according to veteran Hollywood reporter Kyle Buchanan of The New York Times. He said he's "been hearing" that Latukefu got the role, but it's not yet officially confirmed by the studio. Deadline also reported on his casting, going on to say he made a multi-movie deal.
title: The Legend Of Zelda Live-Action Movie May Have Found Its Ganondorf

With Sony ending the production of game discs in January 2028, the PS5 manufacturer has reportedly begun to slap warning stickers on restocks of its console, informing consumers that games will only be available in a digital format 17 months from now.

Spotted by YouTuber Behind the Games--who says the console was purchased by a "trusted source" they know--the sticker includes the following disclaimer:

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
The co-creator of Halo and designer of Master Chief, Marcus Lehto, has weighed in with his thoughts about the latest Halo remake, Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Posting on social media, Lehto said he has been slowly playing through the game on the Heroic difficulty and he has some issues but mostly he's having a great time and is happy with the game.

"Overall, I really love the upgrades: movement, cinematics, visuals. Damn, the lighting is brilliant," he said. "Do I have gripes? A few, but they are taking a back seat to the fun."

As for why he played on Heroic, Lehto
title: Halo Co-Creator Calls Out Remake For Pandering To “New Era Of Players With 0% Attention Span”

description:
At long, long last, a fresh look at GTA 6 is coming later this month--if you have a Netflix subscription. More than a year has passed since Rockstar last uploaded a proper trailer for its highly anticipated open-world game, and on August 27, it'll be a Netflix exclusive for several hours--or several minutes, knowing the current state of the internet.

title: Netflix’s GTA 6 Exclusive Seems Doomed

description:
After a decade of dormancy, the Star Fox franchise has seen a huge push from Nintendo in two significant ways. For starters, Fox McCloud had a pretty big presence in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, which made over $1 billion worldwide at the box office. Then, in June, Star Fox, a remake of Star Fox 64, came out exclusively on Switch 2. However, the strong marketing blitz hasn't seemed to lead to a smash-hit sales success for the game--at least not yet.

author: Mark Delaney
description:
Though it's not the most recent Ghost Recon game, everyone, including even Ubisoft apparently, knows Wildlands is the best in the series, so it's become the domain of the Ghost Recon 25th-anniversary celebration, with a massive free update that's out now. 

The update includes a new mission starring a new villain, a visual overhaul on current-gen consoles, and hundreds of new free customization items. There's more than that to it, so here's everything to know.

Billed as the Last Rites update, Wildlands is now playable in 4K and 60 frames per second on current-gen platforms. The update is free, so you don't need to buy the game on new platforms. If you own the previous version, you already have access and may just need to update your game.

The Last Rites update also adds a new mission--really a mission arc made up of several objectives, based
title: The Best Ghost Recon Just Got A Huge Update, And A New Game Is Coming

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
If you thought PC component prices were bad this year, then 2027 might be even worse for your wallet. According to a new report, three of the biggest manufacturers of PC memory--Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron--are already sold out of the crucial components, as AI companies continue to consume all of the available stock.

DigiTimes (via Tweaktown) says that all DRAM and HBM production for next year has sold out, and the big three have no plans to manufacture additional memory. What's happened here is that demand has exceeded supply, and while the companies continue to cater to corporations that are scaling up their data centers, there's a limit on ho
title: All Of 2027’s RAM Could Already Be Gone As Major Manufacturers Sell Out

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
A developer who worked on Grand Theft Auto 5 has said he "would not be shocked at all" if Rockstar decides to delay GTA 6 yet again.

Speaking to Indy100, Mike York said based on his previous experience working at Rockstar, he believes "they could delay it again."
title: Another GTA 6 Delay Would Not Be Surprising, Former Rockstar Dev Says

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
One of the biggest talking points in gaming lately has been around Sony's decision to end support for physical game discs in 2028. It's prompted concerns about game preservation, along with people generally being upset about owning physical media. Now, publisher Capcom has shared its thoughts, with management saying the shrinking physical game market is not expected to have much of an impact because the company sells mostly digital games.

"Approximately 90% of our unit sales are digital. We do not anticipate a significant impact at this time," the company
title: Capcom Unfazed By Physical Games Dying Off

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The Viture Pro 2 Extended Reality (XR) glasses have been officially revealed, and if you've been looking to adopt this tech for your gaming, then this might be the set to grab, as it's tailored to provide long-lasting comfort, impressive tech, and a nice price tag of $299.

Viture says that it focused on creating its lightest and thinnest XR glasses yet with the Pro 2, as it prioritized comfort and travel-friendly ergonomics. Out of the box, each pair comes with three nose-pad sizes with seven adjustment positions, a detachable lens shade to block ambient light, and a nice travel case to protect the hardware when you're not using it. Internally, the Pro 2 is capable of transmitting 1080p 120Hz video to your eyes, and the Sony micro-OLED lenses can reach 1,600 nits of peak brightness.
title: Viture’s New Pro 2 XR Glasses Want To Be The Ones You Can Wear For Hours

author: Callum Self
description:
The sun is out, forever burning my skin and making me wish for fall. Summer, in my humble opinion, kind of stinks--but if there’s anything that makes it better, it’s sale events like these. Not that I need an excuse to stay indoors, anyway. Steam’s Summer Sale may be long gone by this point, but the Fanatical Summer Sale has only just started, and many of these Steam keys are even cheaper than Valve’s own discounts. Sorry, Steam.

I’ve put together a list of essential additions to your Steam library, from monster-hunting adventures to hack-and-slash spectacles. These are some of my favorite titles of recent years, so now that they’re at their lowest price ever, there’s no excuse not to play them.
title: Forget Steam’s Summer Sale: Here Are Five Must-Play Games You Can Get Even Cheaper

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Back in August 2025, Nintendo increased the price of the original Switch console in accordance with ongoing tariffs, but after the US Supreme Court declared these to be unlawful, it didn't hesitate to claim a refund. With the release of its quarterly earnings (April 1 to June 30) for the current financial year, we now have a clear picture of just how much these refunds helped Nintendo, as it recorded a 52% increase in its operating profits year-on-year, totaling $300 million.

It's worth noting that Nintendo didn't reach this figure purely with tariff refunds, as the company says that "solid software sales and the resulting increase in the proportion of software in net sales" also helped. The US tariffs--that
title: Nintendo’s Profits Jump $300 Million After Tariff Refunds And Strong Software Sales

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Nintendo has posted its latest quarterly financial results--ranging from April 1 to June 30--and while the Switch 2 continues to be the company's fastest-selling system, sales have dropped considerably in the last three months. Overall, Nintendo's operating profit increased 150.5% thanks to higher software revenue and $300 million in US tariff refunds that won't be passed on to consumers.

title: Nintendo Switch 2 Is Still Outpacing The Original Switch By Millions
